translation_notes: 2026-08-28 (re-examined after the interpolated-datatype and surplus-semicolon fixes): classification UNCHANGED (awkward), but for a narrower reason than before. The datatype position is now the documented first-class form `^^{expr}` (language.md: 'the datatype may itself be interpolated, {expr}^^{dt}, for the generic case where the type is computed at run time'), so translated.ldpy line 159 was normalised from the `^^f{...}` formatted-node spelling to `f"{value_components[0]}"^^{DataType.load(value_components[1]).as_xml_uri_ref()}`. Both spellings emit byte-identical code today -- Literal(f"{...}", datatype=dtype(...)) -- so this is a notation cleanup, not a behaviour change; driver re-run, RDFEVAL-VERDICT equivalent (module-state, stdout)

2026-08-28: what the fix did NOT buy, and why awkward stands. The residual wart was never the datatype, it is the LEXICAL side: outside a g{} island the bare `{expr}^^{dt}` form is not recognised (verified -- it is left untouched as Python text), so a runtime value must still be laundered through `f"{v}"` to acquire a ^^ suffix. That laundering stringifies, which is exactly the trap the fix does not remove: it is faithful here only because value_components[0] comes from raw_value.split("^^") and is therefore always a str, so f"{v}" is v. The rewrite is still no shorter and no clearer than the plain RDFLiteral(x, datatype=...) constructor it replaces
2026-08-28: the surplus-semicolon fix is inapplicable -- the translation contains no g{} island at all (0 matches), the region's single RDF op is a term constructor

2026-08-28: dtype() reads a plain string as an IRI, so the form would also be safe if as_xml_uri_ref() returned a str; here it returns a real URIRef (neat_shim.py:136), so the coercion is a no-op either way
--- notes from the first review wave (note 1 below is superseded on the f{...} point by the 2026-08-28 revision above) ---

the region's single RDF operation is RDFLiteral(value_components[0], datatype=DataType.load(value_components[1]).as_xml_uri_ref()) -- a literal whose lexical form AND datatype are both runtime values. It becomes the island f"{value_components[0]}"^^f{DataType.load(value_components[1]).as_xml_uri_ref()}, which transpiles to exactly Literal(f"{...}", datatype=node(...))

negative finding: this is the awkward case for the notation. ldpy's typed-literal syntax needs a *lexical* left-hand side, so a runtime string has to be laundered through an f-string (f"{x}") before it can carry a ^^ suffix, and the dynamic datatype needs the f{...} escape hatch; the result is not shorter and arguably less readable than the plain rdflib constructor. The forms the notation is good at ("4"^^xsd:integer, {v}^^xsd:integer) both require the datatype to be written literally, which this code cannot do because it dispatches on _XSD_TYPES at run time

semantic nuance: f"{x}" stringifies its argument whereas Literal(x) preserves the Python type; here value_components[0] is always a str (a regex group), so the two are identical, but the equivalence is not general

RDFLiteral stays imported on the ldpy side: it is still needed for the field annotation 'value: RDFLiteral | ConceptEntity | NamedIndividualEntity' and for isinstance() tests, so unlike the pySHACL example the island does not retire the import

negative finding: everything else in this 230-line module is pydantic/regex plumbing over an RDF-flavoured *string* syntax ('valueConstraint:p(hasValue,4^^integer)') that is parsed by hand; ldpy has nothing to offer such string-level RDF surface syntax

context shim: neat_shim.py provides behavioural stand-ins for the six names imported from cognite.neat (EntityTypes, _XSD_TYPES, DataType, _PARSE, ConceptEntity/ConceptualEntity, NeatValueError, remove_namespace_from_uri) - the real package pulls in the whole cognite-client SDK. The six import lines were rewritten identically in both representations; the shim is a stand-in, not a copy, and both sides use it identically

demo harness added identically to both representations: the region only defines models, so nothing is observable at import time. It parses the five restriction shapes (including the datatyped-literal one) and prints the results plus the built Literal, its datatype and its Python value; the driver compares the captured stdout

the two model_rebuild() calls at the top of the demo harness are a harness accommodation (the driver exec()s the module in a namespace absent from sys.modules, so pydantic cannot resolve the Literal[...] alias annotations on its own); identical on both sides, no behavioural effect
